High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Order
This first bail application under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (equivalent to Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the applicant Mayaram @ Sandeep Sojatiya for grant of regular bail, who has been arrested on 26/05/2024 in connection with Crime No.49/2024 registered at Police Station Nahar Darwaja, District Dewas (M.P.) for commission of offences under Section 363, 366, 376(2)(n) and 376(3) of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 5(l)
and 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. As per prosecution case, the allegation against the applicant is that he has abducted and committed rape upon the prosecutrix.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against him.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the crime.
There is no sufficient NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:583 2 MCRC-56016-2024 evidence available on record to establish the complicity of the accused with the alleged crime.
He has not committed any offence.
Investigation is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
Even in the statements of prosecutrix, her mother and father recorded before the trial Court, they have not supported the prosecution case.
Final conclusion of the trial will also take considerable long time, therefore, learned counsel prays for allowing the bail application and for grant of bail.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State has vehemently opposed the prayer and prays for dismissal of the bail application on the ground that DNA report is positive and prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident, therefore, application be dismissed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. In the aforesaid factual backdrop coupled with the fact that prosecutrix has not even supported the prosecution case at the time of statement before the Court and issue of age of the prosecutrix is also under dispute, this Court is inclined to grant benefit of bail to the applicant.

Accordingly,
without commenting on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with separate solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by the said Court, without any default, during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:583 3 MCRC-56016-2024 8.
The applicant will not indulge himself in any criminal activity in future.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial
, however, in case of bail jump and / or breach of any of the conditions of bail, this order will come to an end and applicant will be liable to be arrested by the concerned authorities.
9. Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
